system_description.narrative_title: Energy geopolitics reshapes markets ahead of U.S. midterms
system_description.narrative_summary: Diplomatic movement around the Iran conflict and initiatives to restore Russian gas flows are easing oil supply fears, triggering sharp falls in oil prices and ripples across bond, currency and equity markets. That market recoil is interacting with central-bank rate expectations, corporate cost pressures (notably fuel-sensitive sectors) and election-timed political decisions, producing fast feedbacks between diplomacy, energy supply, asset prices and policy responses. The window shows a system recalibrating risk and reallocating capital as geopolitics alters perceived energy scarcity.
system_description.scope: International energy supply and demand (oil and gas flows), diplomatic negotiations and security events in the Middle East and Europe, global commodity and financial markets (oil, bonds, FX, equities, gold), central-bank policy expectations, major energy firms and state energy actors, and election/timing effects on policy choices.
system_description.super_system: Global political-economic system (interplay of geopolitics, energy security, and international capital markets)
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and investor risk appetite
Energy production & infrastructure (producers, pipelines, LNG terminals)

variables.name: Oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price per barrel of crude oil reflecting aggregate supply-demand balance and market participants' valuation.

variables.name: Natural gas flow rate
variables.description: The volumetric rate at which pipeline and LNG systems deliver natural gas across regions and routes.

variables.name: Oil production capacity utilization
variables.description: The proportion of installed upstream oil production capacity that is actively being used to produce crude.

variables.name: Strategic supply buffer levels
variables.description: The quantity of stored energy commodities (oil and refined products) held as reserves or buffers against supply disruptions.

variables.name: Diplomatic negotiation intensity
variables.description: The frequency, scale and intensity of diplomatic engagements aimed at resolving energy-related or regional security disputes.

variables.name: Geopolitical security tension
variables.description: The prevailing level of political and military tension in regions critical to energy supply and trade routes.

variables.name: Market risk perception
variables.description: Investors' and counterparties' aggregate perception of downside risk in financial and commodity markets.

variables.name: Financial market volatility
variables.description: The magnitude and frequency of price swings across major asset classes (equities, bonds, FX, commodities).

variables.name: Bond yield level
variables.description: The prevailing yields on sovereign and core corporate bonds that reflect interest rate, inflation and credit risk pricing.

variables.name: Currency exchange rate level
variables.description: The prevailing nominal exchange rate between major currencies as a reflection of relative monetary and macroeconomic conditions.

variables.name: Monetary policy expectations
variables.description: Market-implied expectations for future central-bank policy rates and the timing of monetary policy shifts.

variables.name: Corporate fuel cost exposure
variables.description: The extent to which firms' operating costs and margins are sensitive to changes in energy (fuel and power) prices.

variables.name: Election-timed policy constraint
variables.description: The degree to which upcoming electoral timing biases fiscal and regulatory decision-making toward short-term or symbolic actions.

variables.name: Capital allocation flow to risk assets
variables.description: The net flow rate of investment capital into riskier asset classes and sectors (equities, commodities, leveraged credit) versus safe assets.

variables.name: Energy infrastructure security
variables.description: The operational integrity and resilience of energy transport, storage and production infrastructure against physical and cyber threats.

variables.name: Speculative derivative positioning
variables.description: The aggregate size and directional bias of leveraged and non-commercial derivative positions in energy and related markets.

catalysts.title: U.S. 2026 midterm elections
catalysts.description: U.S. congressional midterms that will re-shape fiscal, regulatory and geopolitical signalling, driving market positioning and short-term risk sentiment.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Sectors bracing...as US midterm elections loom'; 'Crude oil prices sell off...ahead of U.S. midterms'.

catalysts.title: Doha Iran peace talks progress or deal drafting
catalysts.description: Ongoing diplomatic talks (Doha) and circulated draft proposals that could ease Middle East supply fears and lower oil risk premia.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Oil Drops Amid Diplomatic Efforts to Revive Mideast Peace Talks'; 'Iranians have left Doha talks, draft proposal...'; 'Oil Prices Fall...as Iran Peace Talks Ease Supply Fears'.

catalysts.title: Risk of further U.S.–Iran military escalation
catalysts.description: After reported U.S. strike on Qeshm Island, the risk of retaliatory or follow-up strikes could raise regional tension and energy risk premia.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'U.S. reportedly strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as Vance hopes for ‘negotiated settlement’ with Tehran'.

catalysts.title: Push to restore Russian gas sales to Europe via Ukraine
catalysts.description: Diplomatic and commercial efforts to re-enable Russian gas exports transiting Ukraine, which would materially change European gas flows and prices.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Exclusive | U.S. Pushes to Restore Russian Gas Sales to Europe Via Ukraine'.

catalysts.title: Oleshky ceasefire expiry and frontline shifts in Ukraine
catalysts.description: Expiration of a local ceasefire and reported evacuations/reinforcements in Kherson region, risking renewed fighting and supply-route disruption.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Oleshky ceasefire expires, Ukraine evacuates civilians'; 'Ukraine says Russia used Oleshky ceasefire to reinforce positions'.

catalysts.title: Policy/market responses to eroded global energy buffers
catalysts.description: Public warnings about thin supply buffers (ADNOC) are likely to trigger producer decisions, strategic releases, or buyer hedging that shift short-term markets.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'World's energy supply buffers have been eroded, ADNOC CEO says'.

catalysts.title: Completion of major gas-asset stake deals (TotalEnergies, LNG Canada)
catalysts.description: Closings or progress on announced gas asset transactions that could alter near-term LNG and offshore gas development and capacity plans.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'TotalEnergies to buy 30% stake in two Malaysian offshore gas fields'; 'Blackstone Leads $3.1 Billion Investment in Mitsubishi’s Stake in LNG Canada'.
